title: Files: read and write
hook: Make Python read a crew list and write a log file that is still there tomorrow.

warmup.q: You wrote a function that works out pace once. Why bother with a function?
options: Python will not run without one
You can reuse it for every run without retyping
It makes the answer more accurate
warmup.explain: A function names a set of steps. Write it once, call it as many times as you like.

warmup.q: `int("seven")` would crash with a ValueError. What does `try` / `except ValueError` do?
options: Runs the except block instead of crashing
warmup.explain: The try block is tried. If that error happens, Python jumps to the except block and carries on.
`.get` does not crash on a missing key. It hands back the default you gave it, here `nobody`.

why.heading: Programs forget
why.text: When a program ends, every variable is gone. A crew list stored in a variable is lost the moment you close it. A **file** lives on the disk, so it is still there tomorrow. Files are how a program remembers.

why.heading: Open, use, close
why.text: `with open("crew.txt") as f:` opens the file and calls it `f`. Everything indented under it can use `f`. When the indent ends, Python closes the file for you. Always use `with`, so you never forget to close.

why.heading: Reading
why.text: `f.read()` gives the whole file as one big string. Or loop with `for line in f:` to get one line at a time. Each line still has its **newline** (the invisible line break) on the end, so use `line.strip()` to clean it.

why.heading: Writing
why.text: Add a mode after the name. `"w"` is write: it makes the file and **erases anything already in it**. `"a"` is append: it adds to the end and keeps what was there. Then `f.write("text\n")`. Write adds no line break, so you add `\n` yourself.

why.heading: A file that is not there
why.text: Open a missing file and Python raises `FileNotFoundError`. You know how to deal with errors: wrap it in `try` / `except FileNotFoundError`. A program that checks first beats a program that crashes on set.

watch.intro: Tap Run. It reads three names from crew.txt, writes a log file, then reads the log back.
watch.code:
with open("crew.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print("Crew:", line.strip())
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Crew checked\n")
with open("log.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())
explain: The first `with` reads crew.txt one line at a time. `strip()` removes the hidden line break.
The second `with` uses mode `"w"`. log.txt did not exist, so Python made it.
`f.write` puts text in the file. The `\n` ends the line.
The third `with` reads log.txt back with `read()` to prove it was saved.
watch.break_it: Change `"crew.txt"` on line 1 to `"crews.txt"` and tap Run. Python raises `FileNotFoundError` and says there is no such file. A wrong name is the most common file mistake. Put it back.

tasks.title: Read a note
tasks.task:
The file `note.txt` is already there. Read it and show everything in it. The result is:

`Bring the ND filter.`
`Charge all batteries.`
tasks.starter:
with open("note.txt") as f:
    text = f.read()
# now print text
tasks.solution:
with open("note.txt") as f:
    text = f.read()
print(text)
hints: The text is already in the variable `text`. You only need to show it.
Add one line at the bottom: print the variable `text`.

files.note.txt:
Bring the ND filter.
Charge all batteries.

tests.expect:
Bring the ND filter.
Charge all batteries.

tasks.title: Write a call list
tasks.task:
`names.txt` has one name per line. Make a new file `callsheet.txt` with one line per name, like this:

`Call: Sam`
`Call: Lerato`
`Call: Jo`
tasks.starter:
with open("names.txt") as f:
    names = f.readlines()
with open("callsheet.txt", "w") as out:
    for n in names:
        # write one line here
        pass
tasks.solution:
with open("names.txt") as f:
    names = f.readlines()
with open("callsheet.txt", "w") as out:
    for n in names:
        out.write("Call: " + n.strip() + "\n")
hints: `readlines()` gives a list of lines. Each still ends with a hidden line break, so clean it with `n.strip()`.
Inside the loop use `out.write(...)`. Build the text as "Call: " plus the clean name plus "\n".

expect_files.callsheet.txt:
Call: Sam
Call: Lerato
Call: Jo

tasks.title: Count, then add a line
tasks.task: Open `shots.txt`. If it is there, show `Shots so far: N` (N is the number of lines in it). If it is missing, show `No shots yet`. Either way, then add the line `Slate 9` to the end of `shots.txt`.
tasks.starter:
try:
    with open("shots.txt") as f:
        n = len(f.readlines())
    print("Shots so far:", n)
# add the except, then the append
tasks.solution:
try:
    with open("shots.txt") as f:
        n = len(f.readlines())
    print("Shots so far:", n)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("No shots yet")
with open("shots.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("Slate 9\n")
hints: A `try` must be followed by an `except`. Which error do you catch for a missing file?
After the try / except, start a new `with open("shots.txt", ...)` with no indent. Which mode adds to the end?
Use mode "a" and f.write("Slate 9\n"). The except line is: except FileNotFoundError:

recap: `with open(name) as f:` opens a file and closes it for you.
`f.read()` is the whole file. `for line in f:` is one line at a time. `strip()` cleans each line.
Mode `"w"` erases and writes. Mode `"a"` adds to the end.
`FileNotFoundError` means the name or place is wrong. Catch it with try / except.

words.meaning: Information saved on the disk with a name, so it survives after the program ends.
Opens something, lets you use it in the indented block, then closes it for you.
The letter after the file name: "r" read (the default), "w" write, "a" append.
The hidden line break at the end of each line, written \n.
Add to the end of a file and keep what was already there.
